item.title: An Atiyah-Segal homomorphism for approximate representations of infinite groups, and almost multiplicative ucp maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.24252v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Atiyah-Segal homomorphism relates the representation ring of a finite group to the $K$-theory ring of its classifying space. We develop a version of this for infinite groups, but based on a ring of approximate representations rather than representations. We then use known results on the Baum-Connes conjecture to show that our homomorphism is an isomorphism for many groups: this includes all torsion-free amenable groups, and all torsion-free fundamental groups of compact manifolds of dimension at most three. The main motivation is the desire to understand approximate representations using topological tools: as a sample application we give some examples of torsion phenomena in approximate representation theory. The methods of proof are $C^*$-algebraic: the key idea is to relate our Atiyah-Segal type homomorphism to Kasparov's coassembly map. The main step realizes (Hausdorffized) $KK$-theory as approximately multiplicative ucp maps modulo stable approximate unitary equivalence for appropriate $C^*$-algebras. This is in the spirit of the stable uniqueness theorems of Dadarlat-Eilers and Lin, and may be of purely $C^*$-algebraic interest.
item.dc:creator: Rufus Willett

item.title: An explicit Dennis trace and its compatibility with Koszul duality
item.description: arXiv:2610.25485v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we construct explicit Dennis trace maps from algebraic $K$-theory to Hochschild homology for dg module and curved dg comodule categories, and prove their compatibility with derived Koszul duality. For this, we construct a natural chain map $\tau$ from the chains on the newly defined thickened nerve to the total complex of the dg cyclic nerve, with explicit formulas incorporating morphisms and coherent higher homotopies, which generalizes McCarthy's approach. This $\tau$ construction works both for modules over dg algebras and for cdg comodules over counital conilpotent curved dg coalgebras. Combining the $\tau$ with the dg-enriched Waldhausen $S_\bullet$-construction and a Hochschild delooping theorem yields the Dennis trace maps. For thick subcategories corresponding under derived Koszul duality, we prove that the induced $K$-theory equivalences and Hochschild homology isomorphisms fit into natural commutative diagrams with these trace maps.
item.dc:creator: Maozhou Huang

item.title: Additive invariants of Finite-dimensional DG-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.26302v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Orlov has shown that additive invariants such as K-theory and Hochschild homology of smooth finite-dimensional DG-algebras behave similarly to those of finite-dimensional algebras. The similarities only go so far: there are examples of finite-dimensional DG-algebras with vanishing and uncountable Grothendieck groups. We show that for DG-quivers with relations, the Grothendieck groups are free of the expected rank and that, in the smooth case, all additive invariants are determined by the base field. We use our results to rule out certain finite-dimensional DG-algebras from being phantoms.
item.dc:creator: Isambard Goodbody

item.title: Twisted logarithmic de Rham complexes and the rational hit conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.26028v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the top degree concentration property for the cohomology of twisted logarithmic de Rham complexes of multiarrangements of hyperplanes. Our main tool is a short exact sequence of twisted logarithmic de Rham complexes based on the deletion-restriction exact sequences for logarithmic differential forms found recently by Abe and Denham. We prove a number of general results that can be used to establish the top degree cohomology concentration property, and also establish that property for some families of multiarrangements. As a consequence of our results, we prove the rational hit conjecture of R.~M.~W.~Wood about the coinvariants of the rational Steenrod algebra acting on the polynomial ring. We also make progress on the deformed version of that conjecture proposed by Hivert and Thi\'ery, prove generalizations of the rational hit conjecture for all complex reflection groups $G(m,p,n)$, thus answering questions of Bergeron, Borie and Thi\'ery, and generalize the rational hit conjecture to all standard subalgebras of the rational Steenrod algebra.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Dotsenko

item.title: $\mathbb{C}$-Motivic Eilenberg-Mac Lane Spectra as $\mathrm{MGL}$-Motivic Thom Spectra and Normed $\mathbb{G}_m$-Hochschild Homology
item.description: arXiv:2610.26771v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We exhibit the $p$-complete $\mathbb{C}$-motivic Eilenberg-Mac Lane spectra $\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_p$ and $(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_p^{\wedge}$ as $\mathbb{E_3}$-$\mathrm{MGL}_p^{\wedge}$-motivic Thom spectra over the motivic $\mathbb{G}_m$-loop spaces $\Omega_{\mathbb{G}_m}\mathrm{BGL}$ and $\Omega_{\mathbb{G}_m}\mathrm{BSL}$, respectively. Furthermore, for $p=2$, we compute the $\mathrm{MGL}_2^{\wedge}$-relative $\mathbb{G}_m$-Hochschild Homology $\mathbb{G}_m \odot^{\mathrm{MGL}_2^{\wedge}} {-}$, recently introduced by Bachmann-Burklund-Dundas-{\O}stv{\ae}r, of $\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_2$ and $(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_2^{\wedge}$ to be $\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_2[\mathrm{BGL}]$ and $(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_2^{\wedge}[\mathrm{BSL}]$ as $\mathbb{E}_2$-$\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_2$-algebras and $\mathbb{E}_2$-$(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_2^{\wedge}$-algebras, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Preston Cranford

item.title: Splitting vector bundles over real algebraic varieties
item.description: arXiv:2511.15616v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Suppose $X$ is a smooth affine real variety and $\mathscr{E}$ is a vector bundle over $X$. We analyze the problem of splitting off a free rank one summand from $\mathscr{E}$ in corank $0$ and $1$. The problem in corank $0$ can be viewed as the search for a real analog of Murthy's celebrating splitting theorem in the algebraically closed case: to wit, beyond the vanishing of the top Chern class in Chow theory, are the obstructions to splitting ``purely topological''? In a sense, the answer in this case is yes, and we give a proof, using motivic techniques, of a mild extension of the results of Bhatwadekar-Sridharan and Bhatwadekar-Das-Mandal. In corank $1$, in the algebraically closed situation, Murthy's splitting conjecture (now a theorem in characteristic $0$) predicts that the vanishing of the top Chern class in Chow theory is the only obstruction to splitting off a free rank $1$ summand, and we can search for a suitable ``real'' analog of this assertion. We observe that several natural guesses for a ``real'' analog of Murthy's splitting conjecture cannot be true, i.e., that the situation over the real numbers is rather complicated.
item.dc:creator: Aravind Asok, Jean Fasel, Samuel Lerbet

item.title: Equivalence of categories of bivariant K-theory for C*-algebras over topological spaces via reflection functors
item.description: arXiv:2608.22317v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, for various pairs of topological spaces $X$ and $Y$, we introduce an analogue of the Bern\v{s}te\u{\i}n-Gel'fand-Ponomarev reflection functors between the categories of C*-algebras over $X$ and $Y$. We prove that these functors induce equivalences $\mathfrak{KK}(X)_{\mathrm{loc}} \simeq \mathfrak{KK}(Y)_{\mathrm{loc}}$ between Meyer and Nest's localizing subcategories in Kirchberg's ideal-related KK-theory, and $\mathfrak{E}(X) \simeq \mathfrak{E}(Y)$ between the entire categories in Dadarlat and Meyer's ideal-related E-theory. Both equivalences restrict to the respective bootstrap categories: $\mathcal{B}(X) \simeq \mathcal{B}(Y)$ and $\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{E}}(X) \simeq \mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{E}}(Y)$. Combining these equivalences with a combinatorial argument in quiver representation theory, we obtain the same equivalences for any two finite $T_0$-spaces whose Hasse diagrams are orientations of the same tree. Moreover, we prove a rearrangement property of reflection functors, which yields an analogue of Coxeter functors. Finally, we apply reflection functors to give a conceptual alternative proof of Bentmann and K\"ohler's universal coefficient theorem for filtrated K-theory over finite $T_0$-spaces whose Hasse diagrams are orientations of Dynkin diagrams of type A.
item.dc:creator: Nanami Hashimoto

item.title: Singular equivalences of $n$-adjoint type and standard eventually homological isomorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2609.03365v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We refine the definition of eventually homological isomorphisms so that it becomes more natural and fruitful. We introduce singular equivalences of $n$-adjoint type which can be viewed as standard singular equivalences of different levels and are more convenient for reducing various homological conjectures and transferring homological properties. We develop the theories of singular equivalences of $n$-adjoint type for $n\ge 2$ and standard eventually homological isomorphisms between derived categories by giving their characterizations in terms of $\otimes$-(co)perfect complexes of bimodules, two constructions via opposite algebras and tensor product algebras, examples induced by homomorphisms of algebras and idempotents, and applications to the reduction of homological conjectures such as the finitistic dimension conjecture, Gorenstein symmetry conjecture and Auslander-Reiten conjecture, as well as to the preservation of homological properties such as Gorensteinness, the Fg condition, Happel's property and Han's property. Moreover, we show that essentially surjective standard eventually homological isomorphisms between derived categories correspond to standard singular equivalences with canonical left adjoint.
item.dc:creator: Yang Han, Yongyun Qin, Xianqing Wang

item.title: BV rigidity for compact Lie groups and the integral string topology of the symplectic group
item.description: arXiv:2610.04164v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a connected compact Lie group and $R$ a commutative ring over which $H_*(G;R)$ is an exterior algebra on odd primitive generators. We prove a rigidity theorem: the Batalin-Vilkovisky (BV) algebra $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)$ of Chas and Sullivan on the homology of the free loop space is that of the product of odd spheres with the classical exponents of $G$, tensored with the group ring of the torsion of $\pi_1(G)$. Conversely, over an integral domain the graded algebra $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)$ already determines the exponents and the group ring, hence the BV algebra. If moreover $G$ is simply connected, then $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)$, as a BV algebra, is the Hochschild cohomology of $H^*(G;R)$ with the BV operator induced by Poincar\'e duality. The isomorphism with the product of spheres is algebraic: for $\mathrm{Sp}(n)$, $n\geq2$, and $\mathrm{SU}(n)$, $n\geq3$, no map of spaces induces it over $\mathbb{Z}$. We compute, in Hepworth's presentation, the integral BV algebra $\mathbb{H}_*(L\mathrm{Sp}(n);\mathbb{Z})$ with its Gerstenhaber bracket, open for $n\geq2$, the running example of the rigidity theorem.
item.dc:creator: Mukilraj K (Indian Institute of Science Education,Research Kolkata, India)
